title: The Mermaid Theory
cn: 第 11 集 · 美人鱼理论
novel: Ted's friendship with Zoey was put to the test when Barney introduced the so-called Mermaid Theory. According to Barney, a man could not be just friends with a married woman because eventually he would see her as a [[mermaid|mermaid]]. The theory stated that after a certain amount of time, a man would start to find any woman [[attractive|attractive]], no matter how she looked before. Ted [[dismissed|dismiss]] the idea at first, but the more time he spent with Zoey, the more he worried that Barney might be right. He tried to keep his [[distance|distance]], but Zoey kept reaching out to him. They had long conversations about architecture and art, and Ted felt a deep [[connection|connection]] growing between them. Meanwhile, Marshall and Robin found themselves spending time alone together for the first time. They were both [[nervous|nervous]] because they had heard that men and women could not be just friends. Marshall tried to [[avoid|avoid]] eye contact with Robin, and Robin tried to sit as far away from him as possible. The situation was [[hilarious|hilarious]] and [[awkward|awkward]] at the same time. Eventually, they realized that the theory was [[nonsense|nonsense]] and that they could be friends without any [[romantic|romantic]] tension. Ted, however, was not so lucky. He realized that his feelings for Zoey were growing [[stronger|strong]] every day. He knew that acting on those feelings would [[complicate|complicate]] everything. Zoey was still married to The Captain, and Ted did not want to be the man who broke up a marriage. He [[confided|confide]] in Marshall, who told him to follow his heart but be careful. Ted was [[torn|tear]] between his desire and his principles. The episode ended with Ted and Zoey sharing a quiet moment on a rooftop, looking at the city skyline, both aware that something was [[shifting|shift]] between them but neither willing to name it.

mermaid.en: a imaginary creature with a woman's body and a fish's tail

attractive.en: pleasing to look at or interesting

dismiss.en: to refuse to consider something seriously

distance.en: the amount of space between things

connection.en: a relationship or link between people

nervous.en: feeling worried or anxious about something

avoid.en: to stay away from something or someone

nonsense.en: ideas or words that are silly or untrue

confide.en: to tell someone a private secret

tear.en: to be pulled in different directions
